dish: Dragon soba (ドラゴンそば) — Miyako soba in a bonito-pork broth with Chinese-style chicken stock and chilli heat
w: A Hirara soba shokudō whose house creation is the spicy 'dragon soba', made by adding Chinese-style chicken stock to the bonito-and-pork Miyako soba broth; it also serves a plain Miyako soba. Mapple lists it among Miyako's ten most popular Miyako soba lunch spots.

dish: Asian Miyako soba — Miyako soba broth with aromatic oil, coriander, nira and tomato (pho-style), plus Asian maze-men
n: Cafe Uesuya, Miyako (カフェ ウエスヤ)
w: A creative Asian café opened in 2014 on a Hirara back lane (in the owner's grandfather's former dental clinic) and since relocated within Shimozato, Hirara. At lunch it serves three original takes on Miyako soba; the signature 'Asian Miyako soba' is a pho-like bowl topped with coriander, nira and tomato.

dish: Miyanohana awamori, including organic awamori from chemical-free Japanese rice (since 2006)
n: Miyanohana awamori distillery, Irabu Island (宮の華)
w: Irabu Island's awamori distillery, founded in 1948; its name means 'the eternal flower of Miyako's heart', and around 80% of the staff are women. Besides its Thai-rice awamori it has made an organic awamori from chemical-free Japanese rice since 2006.

dish: Yaeyama soba — thin round noodles in a light pork-and-bonito broth with shredded pork and kamaboko
n: Shima Soba Ichiban-chi Ishigaki Honten (島そば一番地 石垣本店)
w: A Yaeyama-soba specialist named for its address, 'Aza-Ishigaki No. 1', a short walk from Ishigaki port's remote-island terminal (it also has a Naha branch). Tabirai's list of ten must-eat Yaeyama soba shops on Ishigaki includes it, and Rurubu features it.

dish: Yaeyama soba, the dish that won at the first Yaeyama Soba Championship (2015)
n: Café Tēdun Shidamē-kan, Taketomi Island (カフェ てぇーどぅん しだめー館)
w: A red-tiled café beneath the Nagomi-no-tō lookout in Taketomi village, about 12 minutes' walk from the port. It was one of the winners at the first Yaeyama Soba Championship in 2015, the year Komatsu took the Yaeyama-soba grand prix.

n: Ikehara Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (池原酒造)
w: A family awamori distillery in central Ishigaki, founded in 1951, that makes a single brand, Shirayuri ('white lily'). Tabirai profiles it in its series on Okinawa's awamori distilleries.
